items.title: Dow closes at record on Mideast optimism; SpaceX, AMD drag Nasdaq
items.summary:
STORY: U.S. stocks ended mixed on Wednesday, with the Dow adding about half a percent to notch another record high close, the S&P 500 slipping marginally and the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping more than eight-tenths of a percent.

The Nasdaq saw its first decline in five sessions as AMD fell 7% and SpaceX stumbled nearly 14% following the release of its quarterly earnings.

SpaceX shares could face additional pressure from the expiration of the stock's post-IPO lock-up period starting on Thursday, said Shana Orczyk Sissel, founder and CEO of Banríon Capital Management.

"There will likely be a lot of folks looking to sell their positions that they've held for a long time, to monetize their investment, which they've had for a while since the company was private. That's going to put pressure on the stock. [FLASH] So I would not be a buyer of SpaceX until we have a better idea of what kind of float's going to be out there after these lockups expire."

:: Amgen

Outside of tech, shares of Amgen gained about four-and-a-half percent on a second-quarter sales boost for the drugmaker, helping to lift the blue-chip Dow.

Rival Eli Lilly jumped about 5% after the company raised its full-year revenue forecast.

And shares of Disney rose roughly three-and-a-half percent after the entertainment giant beat quarterly profit expectations.
